pr_title: [Fix #13324] Fix `--disable-uncorrectable` to not insert a comment inside a string continuation
pr_body:
With the following code and `--disable-uncorrectable` specified:

```ruby
{
  key1: "something",
  key1: "whatever"\
    "something else",
}
```

Previously RuboCop corrected to a syntax error:

```ruby
{
  key1: "something",
  key1: "whatever"\ # rubocop:todo Lint/DuplicateHashKey
    "something else",
}
```

With this correction, RuboCop uses the block form of `todo` instead:

```ruby
{
  key1: 'something',
  # rubocop:todo Lint/DuplicateHashKey
  key1: 'whatever'\
    'something else'
  # rubocop:enable Lint/DuplicateHashKey
}
```

Fixes #13324.

issue_context.title: --disable-uncorrectable creates syntax errors when violations occur within multi-line strings
issue_context.body:
`--disable-uncorrectable` should not attempt to inject a line-level `rubocop:todo` comment in the middle of a multi-line string.  This results in syntax errors.

This was filed in issue https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/7216 but root cause was not addressed in that issue.  The example cop was just modified to detect fewer violations to work around it.  The general issue of `--disable-uncorrectable` not working correctly with multi-line strings is reproducible with any non-autocorrectable cop that can detect a violation on a line that ends with a string.

Example:

```
# This code has a violation of Lint/DuplicateHashKey

          foo = {
            key1: "something",
            key1: "whatever"\
              "something else",
          }
```


--------

## Expected behavior

`--disable-uncorrectable` should wrap the multi-line string like this:

```
          foo = {
            key1: "something",
            # rubocop:todo Lint/DuplicateHashKey
            key1: "whatever"\
              "something else",
            # rubocop:enable Lint/DuplicateHashKey
          }
```

## Actual behavior

Instead it creates a syntax error

```
          foo = {
            key1: "something",
            key1: "whatever"\ # rubocop:todo Lint/DuplicateHashKey
              "something else",
          }
```


## Steps to reproduce the problem

Create any code sample that has a non-autocorrectable violation of any cop on a line that terminates part-way through a multi-line string.

Run rubocop with `-A --disable-uncorrectable`

## RuboCop version

```
bundle exec rubocop -V
1.66.1 (using Parser 3.3.5.0, rubocop-ast 1.32.3, running on ruby 3.1.3) +server [arm64-darwin21]
  - rubocop-rails 2.10.1
  - rubocop-rspec 2.12.1
  - rubocop-sorbet 0.7.4
  - rubocop-thread_safety 0.5.1

```

review_comments: It seems the test passes even without `range.overlaps?(offense_range)`. Can you review the logic or the test?

`range.overlaps?(offense_range)` is necessary, otherwise string continuations before (but unrelated to) the offense would be captured. I added a second test that would fail without it:

```ruby
context 'and the offense is on a different line than a string continuation' do
  it 'adds a single one-line disable statement' do
    create_file('.rubocop.yml', <<~YAML)
      AllCops:
        DisabledByDefault: true
      Lint/DuplicateHashKey:
        Enabled: true
    YAML
    create_file('example.rb', <<~'RUBY')
      x = 'something'\
        'something else'
      {
        key1: 'foo',
        key1: 'bar'
      }
    RUBY
    expect(exit_code).to eq(0)
    expect(File.read('example.rb')).to eq(<<~'RUBY')
      x = 'something'\
        'something else'
      {
        key1: 'foo',
        key1: 'bar' # rubocop:todo Lint/DuplicateHashKey
      }
    RUBY
  end
end
```
